decision: ALL_COMMON was attempted and abandoned on measured throughput; the run proceeds on FULL_DURATION_64_APPROXIMATION, which is NEVER called 'full sequence'.

measured_throughput.anycalib_scene_predictions: ~0.75 views/min -> ~3.5 h for 157 views (0.17 s/frame model time plus video decode)
measured_throughput.hand_focal_profiles: ~1.5 h real + ~1.5 h wrong-frame control, from the CAM-EXP-006 measured PnP rate at 161 grid points

pre_registered_threshold: spec section 13: report a blocker if new AnyCalib inference exceeds 100,000 frames OR the reasonable runtime estimate exceeds 6 GPU-hours
which_criterion_fired: runtime: ~8 h estimated, above the 6 h threshold. The frame-count criterion did NOT fire (30,031 frames, well under 100,000).
what_was_NOT_done: no arbitrary subsampling of ALL_COMMON was performed. The partial ALL_COMMON caches (9 scene views, 6 reference-3D views) are discarded and contribute to no result.

fallback.name: FULL_DURATION_64_APPROXIMATION
fallback.what: the frozen CAM-EXP-004.1 64-frame grid, which is spread across the whole recording duration by farthest-point insertion in time
fallback.why_cheap: AnyCalib predictions for these exact frames already exist in CAM-EXP-004.1 results/raw/extended_frame_predictions.csv.gz at 100 % success, so NO new scene inference is required
fallback.wording_rule: this must never be described as 'the full sequence'. It is a 64-frame approximation spanning the full duration.
fallback.what_is_unaffected: the primary paired comparison. S0 and S1 still use identical frames, identical scene predictions and identical nuisance parameters; only the hand term differs. The frame-count experiment still covers N=8/16/32/64 nested.
fallback.what_is_affected: the claim about how much temporal evidence a whole video provides. N=ALL_COMMON is not measured.
